simulated_user.persona: a product manager who wants high-level topic areas for a dashboard. The product manager does NOT have strong knowledge of clustering algorithms and how they work.
simulated_user.goal: Separate questions about frameworks/libraries from core language questions.

inputs.user: I want these grouped so that core language questions—covering syntax, built-in types, and standard operators—are kept completely separate from questions about third-party frameworks and libraries like Spring, Hibernate, or Magento. Each cluster should represent either a specific programming language or a specific framework/library category, which will make it much easier to filter the dashboard by what people are actually building versus just how the underlying language works.

outputs.agent:
How should questions about programming language fundamentals (e.g., Scala syntax, C# LINQ, Matlab arrays) be organized relative to each other?

A) Group all language-specific questions into single, unified clusters per language (e.g., one cluster for all Scala questions, one for all C# questions).
B) Merge all "core language" questions from all languages into a single generic "Language Basics" cluster.
C) Group them by abstraction level: "Syntax/Operators" vs "Data Structures/Collections" vs "Advanced Language Features" (across all languages).
D) Keep each question in its own unique cluster (no grouping of language questions together).
E) Other — please describe your preference.

How should questions about "DevOps" or "Tooling" (e.g., SVN, Visual Studio shortcuts, Excel) be handled relative to the "Core Language" vs "Framework" separation?

A) Treat them as a distinct "Tooling/DevOps" category, separate from both Language and Framework clusters.
B) Group them by the specific tool (e.g., one cluster for SVN, one for Visual Studio, one for Excel).
C) Merge them into the "Core Language" cluster, treating tools as part of the developer's environment.
D) Merge them into the "Framework/Library" cluster, treating tools as extensions to the core language.
E) Other — please describe your preference.

How should questions about web platforms and CMSs (e.g., WordPress, Magento, Drupal, SharePoint) be grouped?

A) Group them by the specific platform/CMS (e.g., one cluster for all WordPress questions, one for all Magento questions).
B) Merge all web platform/CMS questions into a single "Web Platforms & CMS" cluster.
C) Group them by the type of technology used (e.g., PHP-based vs. Java-based).
D) Keep each platform in its own unique cluster (no grouping of platform questions together).
E) Other — please describe your preference.

How should questions related to Enterprise Java frameworks (specifically Spring and Hibernate) be grouped relative to each other, given your rule that they must be separate from core language questions?

A) Merge all Spring-related questions into one "Spring Framework" cluster and all Hibernate-related questions into one "Hibernate/JPA" cluster.
B) Merge all Spring and Hibernate questions into a single "Enterprise Java Frameworks" cluster.
C) Separate them not just by framework, but also by role (e.g., "DI/Inversion of Control" vs "ORM/Data Access").
D) Group them by the specific version or edition (e.g., "Spring Security" vs "Spring MVC").
E) Other — please describe your preference.

How should questions about database systems and data manipulation (e.g., Oracle, SQL Server, Excel data lookup) be organized?

A) Group them by the specific database or tool (e.g., one "Oracle" cluster, one "SQL Server" cluster, one "Excel" cluster).
B) Merge all database-related questions into a single "Database & Data Storage" cluster.
C) Separate them by abstraction level: "SQL/Querying" vs "Configuration/Installation".
D) Group them by the ecosystem they are most often associated with (e.g., Java-DB, .NET-DB).
E) Other — please describe your preference.

How should questions about simulation or scientific computing tools (e.g., Simulink) be handled, given they are neither core language syntax nor a standard web framework/library?

A) Create a separate "Scientific Computing & Simulation" cluster.
B) Group them with the "DevOps/Tooling" cluster as specialized software tools.
C) Merge them into the "Core Language" cluster if they interact closely with the language syntax.
D) Group them with the "Framework/Library" cluster as specialized domain libraries.
E) Other — please describe your preference.

outputs.instruction:
Instruct: Cluster StackOverflow question titles by grouping queries about core programming language syntax and features into separate clusters per language, specific third-party frameworks or libraries into their own distinct clusters per technology, specific platforms or CMSs into separate clusters per system, database and data tools into clusters per specific tool, and simulation or scientific computing tools into a dedicated category, ensuring that tooling and devops utilities form their own separate group distinct from language and framework topics.

This approach ensures that documentation is organized by the specific ecosystem or product being discussed, facilitating precise filtering by the subject matter.
